study type: Secondary analysis of a prospective, longitudinal quality improvement study
exposure: Implementation of an Enhanced Recovery After Cesarean (ERAC) protocol
cohort: The study included 308 patients undergoing cesarean delivery (CD), excluding those requiring general anesthesia, with significantly complicated CD, or chronic pain disorders.
finding: Implementation of an ERAC protocol did not significantly change the incidence of postoperative urinary retention, but it significantly decreased the duration of Foley catheter placement after cesarean delivery.
